name: Chengdu
meta_description: TDSC investigative consulting in matters touching Chengdu: electronics supply chain diligence, Sichuan free trade zone partners and foreign-related disputes.
hero_lede: Chengdu is the commercial capital of western China, with large electronics, automotive and services sectors and a provincial free trade zone. TDSC scopes investigative consulting from Nashville for matters touching the city, using lawful public sources and coordinating qualified local professionals and counsel where required.
intro: Chengdu, the capital of Sichuan Province, had a resident population of about 21.5 million in 2024 and a gross regional product of about 2.35 trillion yuan, according to a JETRO overview published in 2025. Services account for most of its output, while manufacturing concentrates in electronics, machinery and equipment, automobiles, medical and health products and new materials. Foreign manufacturers and service firms present in the city include Intel, Dell, Foxconn, Toyota, Volkswagen, Siemens and Bosch. With Chongqing it forms the Chengdu-Chongqing economic circle, which Chinese officials describe as a major centre of laptop, tablet, smartphone and vehicle production for western China.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to Chengdu because it sits at the junction of global electronics supply chains, inland logistics and a growing services economy. A component supplier may be one of several affiliated companies registered in different districts; a distributor may route goods through bonded zones or the city's railway port; a joint venture partner may have local government shareholders or related parties that are not obvious from a contract. Buyers, investors and litigators need to understand who controls these counterparties, how they are connected and what disputes or penalties appear in the public record, while respecting China's restrictions on personal information and data leaving the country.

matters.title: Electronics supplier and contract manufacturer diligence
matters.text: Electronics assembly and component supply around Chengdu involves layered subcontracting. We review registration data, shareholders of record, administrative penalties, litigation and media to identify who controls a supplier, its affiliates and whether subcontracting or quality disputes have surfaced before a purchase order or investment.

matters.title: Joint venture partner background research
matters.text: Chengdu joint ventures frequently involve local state-owned or district-backed shareholders. We map ownership chains, related companies and key individuals' business affiliations from lawful public sources so clients understand whose interests sit behind a partner and where conflicts of interest may arise.

matters.title: Free trade zone and bonded logistics
matters.text: Trading and logistics companies registered in the Sichuan Pilot Free Trade Zone or bonded areas can move goods quickly through air and rail channels. We examine their registration history, customs-related penalties where published, trading links and counterparties to test for diversion, misdescription or undisclosed related parties.

matters.title: Distributor and channel integrity reviews
matters.text: Brands selling into western China often rely on Chengdu distributors. We look at the distributor's ownership, related companies, litigation and complaints to identify grey-market activity, unauthorised sub-distributors, counterfeit links or conflicts with employees of the client before or after termination.

matters.title: Support for foreign-related disputes
matters.text: Disputes before the Chengdu International Commercial Tribunal or in arbitration often turn on corporate history and asset information. We support counsel with research into the opposing party's group structure, published judgments and enforcement records, scoped to what Chinese law allows to be collected and used.

local_context.title: Chengdu International Commercial Tribunal
local_context.text: The Chengdu International Commercial Tribunal was established on 22 April 2022 as part of the Chengdu Intermediate People's Court. It was the third international commercial tribunal in a local people's court, after Suzhou and Beijing, and the first in central and western China. It hears first-instance foreign-related civil and commercial cases from across Sichuan Province under centralised cross-regional jurisdiction, excluding categories such as family, labour, maritime and environmental cases.

local_context.title: Arbitration in Chengdu
local_context.text: The China International Economic and Trade Arbitration Commission (CIETAC) opened its Sichuan Sub-commission and a Sichuan Free Trade Zone Arbitration Center in Chengdu in November 2017, alongside a CCPIT free trade zone service and mediation centre. A municipal arbitration commission also operates in the city. Contracting parties choose the institution; we tailor research to the procedural rules of the forum counsel has selected.

local_context.title: Sichuan Pilot Free Trade Zone
local_context.text: The China (Sichuan) Pilot Free Trade Zone covers about 120 square kilometres in three areas: the Chengdu Tianfu New Area zone, including a high-tech comprehensive bonded zone and airport bonded logistics centre; the Chengdu Qingbaijiang Railway Port area, focused on international distribution, bonded logistics, imported vehicles and links to Belt and Road markets; and the South Sichuan port area at Luzhou. Companies in these zones are subject to specific customs and bonded-area regimes.

local_context.title: Local registration and records
local_context.text: Companies in Chengdu register with district and municipal market regulation authorities, and their core registration data, shareholders of record and administrative penalties appear in the national enterprise credit publicity system. Judgments from Chengdu courts appear in national databases where published. Personal information is protected by national law, so research on individuals is limited to lawful public sources and proportionate to the purpose agreed with counsel.

tdsc_approach: TDSC has no office in Chengdu and works on Chengdu matters from Nashville. We begin with the client's counsel to define the purpose, whether supplier or partner diligence, a distributor concern, or support for a dispute in the Chengdu International Commercial Tribunal or arbitration. Research draws on lawful public sources: enterprise credit publicity data, published judgments and enforcement records, free trade zone and customs information where published, and Chinese-language media. Where local enquiries are needed, we coordinate qualified local professionals and PRC counsel, and we do not use pretexting or restricted government data. We plan data handling around China's personal information and cross-border transfer rules, and our reports set out sources and confidence levels.

faqs.q: Which court hears foreign-related commercial cases in Chengdu?
faqs.a: First-instance foreign-related civil and commercial cases from across Sichuan are generally heard by the Chengdu International Commercial Tribunal, part of the Chengdu Intermediate People's Court, established in April 2022. Some categories, such as family, labour, maritime and environmental cases, are excluded. Counsel should confirm jurisdiction for the specific claim; we scope research to the forum chosen.

faqs.q: Is there an international arbitration institution in Chengdu?
faqs.a: Yes. CIETAC opened a Sichuan Sub-commission and a Sichuan Free Trade Zone Arbitration Center in Chengdu in November 2017, and a municipal arbitration commission also operates locally. Parties choose the institution in their contract. We support counsel with background research on parties and assets for arbitration and for later enforcement through the courts.

faqs.q: How can we check a Chengdu electronics supplier before placing orders?
faqs.a: We start with registration data, shareholders of record, administrative penalties and litigation, then trace affiliated companies that may handle production or exports. Media and industry sources help identify labour, quality or intellectual property disputes. Site visits or interviews, where needed, are carried out by qualified local professionals within PRC law and coordinated with counsel.

faqs.q: What does a Sichuan free trade zone registration tell us?
faqs.a: It shows that a company is registered in a designated zone, such as the Tianfu New Area or Qingbaijiang Railway Port areas, which may give it access to bonded logistics and specific customs procedures. It does not confirm substance or ownership. We look at the company's actual operations, related parties and trading history alongside its registration.

faqs.q: Can personal data gathered in Chengdu be sent to the United States?
faqs.a: Chinese law restricts the collection of personal information and its transfer abroad, and some transfers require specific mechanisms. We agree with counsel at the outset what personal information is necessary, how it will be handled and whether reports can be prepared in a way that limits cross-border transfer of personal data.
